title: Global debt, AI risks among 5 financial stability threats, says RBI Governor Malhotra
key_facts: Reserve Bank of India governor Sanjay Malhotra, speaking at the Kautilya Economic Conclave in New Delhi on Saturday 3 Oct 2026, named five global financial-stability risks: high debt, stretched asset valuations, high leverage, private credit and AI-amplified cyber risk

On valuations he said the AI investment cycle has driven big equity gains and any slowdown in AI investment or earnings could trigger a sharp repricing, worsened by leverage and falling cash flow at major AI firms
He said hedge funds, option sellers and ETFs in advanced economies have raised leverage in equities and bonds, and bank-nonbank links have deepened
On AI he said the most immediate concern is cyber risk, plus model risk, third-party dependence and erosion of human oversight
He said each risk alone is not yet alarming but together they could pressure the global financial system; India is navigating from strength
quote_evidence: "Each of these five risks individually, as I mentioned, may not be a matter of concern as of now, but simultaneous occurrence of these shocks can put significant pressure on the global financial architecture," he said on Saturday.
"The emergence of AI has heightened cyber risks, model risks, third-party dependence, and erosion of human oversight and accountability."
why_it_matters_hint: A major central bank adds its voice to the week's warnings on AI valuations and AI-driven cyber risk
notes: Public speech reported by Hindustan Times' own senior editor.
